1	import { createClient } from "@/lib/supabase/server";
2	import type { LookDraft, WeatherPayload } from "@/lib/generator/types";
3	
4	/**
5	 * The cache read for "Style an outfit with this".
6	 *
7	 * `outfits_styled_unique (user_id, styled_item_id, generated_on, styled_index)`
8	 * scopes the set to one piece per local day, so this is the whole cache: a hit
9	 * costs one indexed lookup and NO model call.
10	 *
11	 * Ordered by `styled_index`, which is the set's own ordinal — NOT `look_index`,
12	 * which styled rows keep NULL so they cannot collide with the daily drop's
13	 * unique index. `nullsFirst` so a row written before the set existed (index
14	 * NULL) still reads as the first look rather than vanishing off the end.
15	 */
16	export async function loadStyledLooks(
17	  userId: string,
18	  itemId: string,
19	  generatedOn: string,
20	): Promise<string[]> {
21	  const supabase = await createClient();
22	  const { data } = await supabase
23	    .from("outfits")
24	    .select("id, styled_index")
25	    .eq("user_id", userId)
26	    .eq("styled_item_id", itemId)
27	    .eq("generated_on", generatedOn)
28	    .order("styled_index", { ascending: true, nullsFirst: true });
29	  return (data ?? []).map((r) => r.id);
30	}
31	
32	/**
33	 * Which pieces the user has already been shown for this styling today.
34	 *
35	 * Feeds `Ctx.recentlyShown` on a "try another", so the next set sinks what was
36	 * just rejected instead of returning it again — the PR #15 bug, in the styled
37	 * path. A soft penalty, never a filter.
38	 */
39	export async function loadStyledPieceIds(
40	  userId: string,
41	  itemId: string,
42	  generatedOn: string,
43	): Promise<string[]> {
44	  const ids = await loadStyledLooks(userId, itemId, generatedOn);
45	  if (!ids.length) return [];
46	  const supabase = await createClient();
47	  const { data } = await supabase.from("outfit_items").select("item_id").in("outfit_id", ids);
48	  return (data ?? []).map((r) => r.item_id);
49	}
50	
51	/**
52	 * Drop a piece's styled set for the day.
53	 *
54	 * Delete-then-insert, for the same reason `saveDailyLooks` does it: a fresh run
55	 * may return a different number of looks, and leftovers must not survive beside
56	 * the new set. `outfit_items` first — the rows hang off `outfits`.
57	 */
58	export async function clearStyledLooks(
59	  userId: string,
60	  itemId: string,
61	  generatedOn: string,
62	): Promise<void> {
63	  const supabase = await createClient();
64	  const ids = await loadStyledLooks(userId, itemId, generatedOn);
65	  if (!ids.length) return;
66	  await supabase.from("outfit_items").delete().in("outfit_id", ids);
67	  await supabase.from("outfits").delete().in("id", ids);
68	}
69	
70	/**
71	 * Persist a styled SET and return the ids, in order.
72	 *
73	 * `look_index` is deliberately left NULL: `outfits_daily_unique` covers
74	 * (user_id, occasion, generated_on, look_index), and Postgres treats NULLs as
75	 * distinct, so two pieces styled on the same day for the same occasion cannot
76	 * collide. The set's own order lives in `styled_index`.
77	 * `loadDailyLooks`/`saveDailyLooks` filter these rows out entirely.
78	 */
79	export async function saveStyledLooks(
80	  userId: string,
81	  itemId: string,
82	  occasion: string,
83	  generatedOn: string,
84	  weather: WeatherPayload,
85	  looks: LookDraft[],
86	): Promise<string[]> {
87	  const ids: string[] = [];
88	  for (const [i, look] of looks.entries()) {
89	    const id = await saveOne(userId, itemId, occasion, generatedOn, weather, look, i);
90	    if (id) ids.push(id);
91	  }
92	  return ids;
93	}

95	async function saveOne(
96	  userId: string,
97	  itemId: string,
98	  occasion: string,
99	  generatedOn: string,
100	  weather: WeatherPayload,
101	  look: LookDraft,
102	  styledIndex: number,
103	): Promise<string | null> {
104	  const supabase = await createClient();
105	
106	  const { data: row } = await supabase
107	    .from("outfits")
108	    .insert({
109	      user_id: userId,
110	      occasion,
111	      generated_on: generatedOn,
112	      styled_item_id: itemId,
113	      styled_index: styledIndex,
114	      look_name: look.name,
115	      ai_reasoning: look.why,
116	      weather_snapshot: weather,
117	      layout: {
118	        anchorIndex: look.anchorIndex,
119	        pieces: look.pieces.map((p) => ({ itemId: p.itemId, slot: p.slot })),
120	      },
121	    })
122	    .select("id")
123	    .single();
124	  if (!row) return null;
125	
126	  const links = look.pieces.map((p) => ({
127	    outfit_id: row.id,
128	    item_id: p.itemId,
129	    slot: p.category,
130	  }));
131	  if (links.length) await supabase.from("outfit_items").insert(links);
132	
133	  return row.id;
134	}

content.text: I've read every changed file plus the new dependency (`loadStyledLooks`). Let me trace the flow one more time for any auth/authz concern.

Analysis complete. The change is a small UX fix:

**Flow trace:**
- `page.tsx` calls `loadStyledLooks(user.id, item.id, today)`. `user.id` comes from `supabase.auth.getUser()` (trusted). `item.id` was already validated by an authenticated fetch upstream. `today` is derived from the authenticated user's own profile timezone.
- `loadStyledLooks` scopes its query with `.eq("user_id", userId)` — no cross-tenant leakage possible; a foreign item id can only ever yield `false`.
- The resulting `styledToday: boolean` is threaded through `ItemDetail` → `StyleCta` and used solely as the initial state of a "Try another look" button's visibility. No shell/SQL/HTML/render sink; the value is a pure boolean.
- No new authorization decision, no new attacker-controllable field reaching any new sink, no logging/telemetry additions, no allowlist/permission change, no fail-open path.

Sibling-path parity: the only decision this boolean gates is a client-side rendering flag. The server-side action `styleWithItem` (invoked by the button) enforces its own authorization independently and is unchanged.

No security issues introduced by this diff.
